chunks: They want you to hasten the evil before the good, even when there have been examples of retribution before them. Though certainly your Lord forgives human beings for their iniquities, your Lord is severe of retribution.

key_terms.السَّيِّئَةُ: The evil (often referring to punishment or a specific event)
key_terms.الْحَسَنَةُ: The good (often referring to reward or gradual revelation)

ai.seo_question: What does the Quran mean by hastening the evil before the good?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the Quraysh's impatience for divine retribution (often interpreted as the punishment of the disbelievers) before the establishment of the believers' reward, reflecting their demand for immediate signs. It underscores the dual attributes of Allah as both All-Forgiving despite human oppression and Severe in Punishment, serving as a reminder of the fate of earlier nations like the people of Noah and Hud. This duality reinforces the concept of divine justice, where patience is required for the gradual unfolding of truth and consequence.
